q7.answer: The document does not define how workers learn of a mode change: they read billing_mode from the config service, but the polling, caching and staleness bound are open (A32). It also does not say what happens to an invoice in process at the switch. The intent row stops a second charge to the same customer-period, but a stale read can still let the wrong engine charge, and no step re-checks billing_mode before a charge.

q8.answer: The evidence sits in the controller's gate record (shadow streak days and invoices, both_entered_at, new_only_entered_at, finance_signoff) plus the per-date count rows from the nightly comparison. The controller refuses a forward move unless its gate check passes, so it cannot promote early through the controller. The doc does not say who may give Finance sign-off, or whether the config service restricts direct writes to billing_mode.

q9.answer: The controller itself evaluates the automatic trigger, with no separate component sending a request. It measures the new-engine charge failure rate per 10-minute window, and when that rate is above 2 percent in both or new_only it starts a rollback as an on-call request would, recording rollback_source as automatic:charge_failure_rate. The data path the controller reads, the window rule and the minimum charge count are still open.

q10.answer: billing_mode keeps its pre-rollback value until hand off, and the charging rule decides who charges. From shadow the old engine keeps charging throughout. From both or new_only neither engine charges, so due periods wait, and catch-up charges nothing. After hand off the old engine charges the unsettled due periods at their ledger amounts, skipping settled ones.

q11.answer: Before any provider call an engine makes a conditional insert of an intent row keyed by customer ID and billing period ID, and only the engine whose insert succeeds may charge. Settled ledger entries are checked and drain or verify settles any charge already confirmed by the provider. The idempotency key is derived from customer and period only, so every attempt sends the same key, which is a second line of protection. The conditional insert needs a unique constraint on the ledger, which the brief does not confirm.

q12.answer: A failed step sets rollback_status to halted and records rollback_step and rollback_last_error, and billing_mode does not change. Charging follows the charging rule: the old engine keeps charging in shadow, while in both or new_only nobody charges and due periods wait. On-call resume reruns the recorded step, and steps are idempotent, so a partial hand off (billing_mode already old_only, flag still set) is completed by rerunning hand off.
